question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class outbound recipient allowlist for Slack only or for shared message channels, and where should enforcement live?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent authorization boundary, config name, default behavior, and upgrade semantics are product/security choices that should not be guessed by an automated fix.

options.title: Design shared outbound target policy
options.body: Add an explicit `allowTo`-style policy with current behavior preserved when unset, shared enforcement before delivery, docs, schema coverage, and focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Ship a Slack-only plugin policy
options.body: Keep scope narrow by adding Slack-owned outbound recipient enforcement first, accepting that other human-chat channels will need separate follow-up.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Treat outbound DM restriction as operator process or external sandbox policy rather than OpenClaw configuration, and close the related hardening requests consistently.

recommendation.title: Design shared outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit `allowTo`-style policy with current behavior preserved when unset, shared enforcement before delivery, docs, schema coverage, and focused upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The related issue triage and Slack policy/outbound history make this the best available routing owner for the security/product boundary choice.
